items.label: text
items.text: A sample of sea water has a concentration of sodium chloride of 35.1 g/dm³. Find its concentration in mol/dm3. (A: Na = 23, Cl = 35.5)

items.label: text
items.text: 1 mol NaCl has a mass of 58.5g.

items.label: text
items.text: There are 35.1 g in every dm³ of solution

items.label: text
items.text: mass(g) number of moles = mass of 1 mole(g)

items.label: text
items.text: Therefore there are 0.600mol in every dm³ of solution and the concentration of the NaCl is 0.600 mol/dm³.

items.label: section_header
items.text: EXAMPLE 1

items.label: text
items.text: What is the concentration of a 0.050 mol/dm³ solution of sodium carbonate, Na2CO3, in g/dm³? (A: C = 12, O = 16, Na = 23)

items.label: text
items.text: 1 dm³ of solution contains 0.050 mol Na2CO3.

items.label: text
items.text: 1 mol Na2CO₃ weighs 106g.

items.label: text
items.text: 1 dm³ of solution contains 5.3g Na2CO, therefore the concentration is 5.3g/dm³.

items.label: section_header
items.text: EXAMPLE 2

items.label: text
items.text: What is the concentration in mol/dm³ of a solution containing 2.1 g of sodium hydrogencarbonate, NaHCO₃, in 250 cm³ of solution? (A,: H = 1, C = 12, O = 16, Na = 23)

items.label: text
items.text: 1 mol NaHCO₃has a mass of 84 g.

items.label: text
items.text: This is in a volume of 250 cm³ but we need to find out how much there is in 1 dm³ (1000 cm³). There are four lots of 250 cm³ in 1000 cm³. Each portion of 250 cm³ contains 0.025 mol, therefore there must be 4 × 0.025 = 0.10mol in 1000cm³.

items.label: text
items.text: The concentration is 0.10mol/dm³.
